correctness.rationale: On a connected sink-free graph a period-two return forces the two-step firing-count vector into the Laplacian kernel; primitive period two forces exactly one firing per vertex. For a phase assignment, the admissible chip-height interval at vertex v has exactly k_v=#opposite-phase neighbors integers; the inequalities are necessary and sufficient. On the corona C_n with r>=1 leaves/core vertex, leaf phase is forced opposite core with one height choice, while core contributes r+e_(i-1)+e_i for binary cyclic edge cuts e_i. Closed spin words correspond to even-parity cuts, two spin lifts cancel temporal two-phase division, giving P_{n,r}(z)=1/2[tr(T_r(z)^n)+tr(T_r(-z)^n)]. T_r(1) has trace 2(r+1), determinant -1; T_r(-1) has double eigenvalue -1, so N_{n,r}=1/2[(r+1+sqrt((r+1)^2+1))^n+(r+1-sqrt(...))^n]+(-1)^n. Independent edge-cut enumerations yielded n=3,4,5 at r=1 counts 37,162,681, n=4,r=2 count 722, and n=5,r=3 count 17683. The inspected supplied verifier additionally specifies six microscopic finite checks; that log alone is not infinite proof. A bounded h_v<2d_v enumeration is exhaustive only for primitive two-cycles by the proved intervals.

value.rationale: Labelled period-two orbit counts are natural dynamical invariants of a conservative synchronous chip-firing automaton; the uniform-leaf-decorated cycle is a canonical unicyclic family. The polynomial completely resolves the core disagreement interfaces and determines an r-independent parity term despite r-dependent exponential growth, a structural distinction invisible to a general period-return criterion. The all-(n,r) exact enumeration is not an arbitrary small graph table.
